issue.body: ### 1. Purpose Extend an existing capability of retrieving Pull Request Information via the GitHub REST API. Currently, users are able to extract some from pull requests, however not all data points have been retrievable. There are multiple points of interest that may be a valuable asset to implement in order to capture the development process (process mining), is extracting formation from pull requests in GitHub. On GitHub, reviewers are able to add comments to lines of code by clicking a plus icon on the left hand side of the code. There, they may write critiques and comments and have the option of simply adding one single comment to that code, or continuing an entire review that consolidates multiple lines of code for the assignee to iterate over. Finishing a review can be done on the top right of the file review page. Users can now add comments to an entire review, approve the pull request in order to be merged, or request changes for the assignee to fix. ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1019d091-db72-409b-b18e-4d34211da462) Here, the lower portion shows the comment endpoint while the top is the review endpoint. Currently, the review endpoint is not implemented in Kaiaulu. The review endpoint (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/reviews) is able to get the 'state' of the review, either APPROVED, COMMENTED, or CHANGES_REQUESTED. https://api.github.com/repos/sailuh/kaiaulu/pulls/295/reviews The review endpoint as noted here: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-comments-for-a-pull-request-review List View: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/reviews Individual Review: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/reviews/{review_id}/comments For in-line code comments, the comments endpoint connected with the pull number is used. https://api.github.com/repos/sailuh/kaiaulu/pulls/295/comments GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/comments ### 2. issue.title: Pulling Request Comment via GitHub REST API

milestone.title: ics496-fall24-m2

issue.body:
### Purpose
--------------
As of now, users are able 2 different endpoints to extract data from pull requests (pull_request and issue_or_pr_request). However, neither of the endpoints extract the in-line comments from pull requests, which can be a point of interest for the user to study.

While the `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/comments/` endpoint does retrieve the comments for pull requests, it does not retrieve the in-line code.

### Process
-------------
To extract this data, we can use an endpoint from Github's REST API.
The particular endpoint being used is: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments`
The documentation for this endpoint can be found on the [Github Page](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/comments?apiVersion=2022-11-28#about-pull-request-review-comments).
The field `"diff_hunk":` is a field unique to this particular endpoint and is what contains the in-line code that the pull request comment is referencing. The diff_hunk field refers to the hunk of code in pull requests that contain the +/- changes made to a particular file. If the comment is referencing a line of code within a hunk, the diff_hunk will contain all lines of code from the start of the hunk, ending with the line of code the comment is referencing.
The diff_hunk field will return null if the review comment was not referencing any lines of code.
The `pull_request_review_id` field returns an integer value that ties the comment to the the Review endpoint.
A parser function will also be needed to turn the resulting JSON file into a more readable table.

### Task List
--------------
- [x] Retrieve the pull request comment from the api endpoint
- [x] Create a downloader for the JSON files
- [x] Create a refresher function for the endpoint
- [x] Create a parser the JSON for `diff_hunk` field to retrieve the in-line code

### Limitations
---------------
This issue implements the pull request Comments endpoint [url](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/comments?apiVersion=2022-11-28_)
We noticed that the process of requesting changes or accepting review, the associated comment with accept/reject is not captured as a review comment in this endpoint.
The Review Endpoint comment for accept/reject groups the comments obtained by the Review Comment endpoint.

issue.body: As part of the thesis done by Haotian using Kaiaulu, we want to integrate the pre-processing functions that export the comment data back in Kaiaulu. The sentiment classifier itself, as is done in Python and is a system of its own, will live in a separate repo: https://github.com/sailuh/sentiment_classifier ------ Referenced from https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/issues/346#issuecomment-3387514587 ## R/jira.R **parse_jira(jira_issue_comments_path)** - parses a folder of JIRA issue JSON files and returns a named list with two elements, issues and comments, where each element is a data.table containing the relevant issue or comment fields standardized for further processing. **parse_jira_replies_with_comment(data)** (To be replaced with parse_jira_replies()) - Called in parse_jira_replies_with_comment(parse_jira(jira_issue_comments_path)) - The currently defined parse_jira_replies() seems identical and can replace it in this call, since it combines issues and comments into one table with the required columns (reply_id, reply_subject, reply_body, etc.) for further cleaning and analysis. - Recommended to delete the defined function "parse_jira_replies_with_comment(data)" and replace where it's called with "parse_jira_replies()" ## R/github.R **parse_github_replies(github_issue_path)** - parses GitHub issues, pull requests, comments, and commits from JSON files, and puts them all into one table with columns like who wrote it, the message, and the subject so it’s ready to use. ## R/mail.R **parse_mbox(perceval_path, mbox_path)** - parses an mbox email archive using Perceval, extracts key fields like message ID, sender, recipients, subject, and body, and returns a standardized data.table with consistently renamed columns for further processing. ## R/sentiment_clean.R **clean_jira_data(data)** - Removes bot-generated messages and 'Hudson' from the JIRA dataset. **clean_mbox_data(data, if_clean_vote=FALSE)** (Rename: filter_irrelevant_mbox_messages()) - Removes automated or irrelevant entries from mbox email data such as system-generated messages, Jira or GitHub notifications, and optional vote-related messages. **clean_mbox_comment(data)** (Rename: remove_invalid_or_duplicate_mbox_comments()) - Removes duplicate rows and any comment whose reply_subject doesn’t match a real reply_id in the dataset. **process_mbox_data(data)** (Rename: clean_and_prepare_mbox_subjects()) - Cleans and standardizes mbox email reply subjects, handling encoding issues and removing common prefixes like "Re:". **create_if_comment_column(data)** (Rename: mark_and_uniquify_comments()) - Adds an if_comment column. It marks a row as a comment when its reply_id is different from its reply_subject, and gives each such comment a unique ID so they can be distinguished from each other ## Misc Note: I've given possible function renames but can still be subjected to change. Additionally, all 3 pre-processing functions located in the sentiment_classifier repo in [filter.py](https://github.com/sailuh/sentiment_classifier/pull/2/files#diff-416889f8bad02bdeeb81399a11737cc761a70bce32334210b6bf10d5bd70db96); remove_punctuation(), clean_text(), and remove_markdown_content() can be refactored and move into R/sentiment_clean.R in order to keep the python notebooks as machine-learning only, keeping in mind that perhaps not all 3 of the pre-processing may be necessary to be placed in Kaiaulu, or that the code blocks of each function can be refactored into some existing R/sentiment_clean.R functions. Can think about this more thoroughly in the future. In this visualization, there are 4 files currently located in Kaiaulu. Within those boxes, represents the the 9 user-defined function calls (not including Base R library function calls) that would be integrated into Kaiaulu + 3 of the pre-processing functions in filter.py located in the sentiment_classifier repo. (Note: Some functions mentioned like parse_jira already exists within the file, they are here for reference since they were also called in the provided notebook) ## Post-meeting issue specification for 10/24/25 @carlosparadis Refactor Kaiaulu’s data pipeline to eliminate .csv dependencies and establish consistent abstractions for Capabilities and Data. # Goals - Remove .csv dependencies (Call R exec functions via subprocess.run() in python notebook) - Kaiaulu exec should support filtered data export for each platform independently (GitHub, JIRA, Mail). - Column Mapping — Determine if the Python notebook needs a helper function in the api folder to rename and map columns so R output matches notebook expectations. (If R outputs y columns and the notebook expects x, map y → x using a Python “mapper” function.) - Refactor R filters — ensure single responsibility and consistent use of reply-table input/output. - Refactor Python filters — align with new reply-table abstractions and remove .csv assumptions. ## Post-meeting issue specification for 10/30/25 @carlosparadis - Create a new function in the api folder of the sentiment_classifier repo that maps certain columns of a reply table to columns that the python sentiment classifier notebook expects (Python notebook expects "Text" and "Polarity" columns) - clean_mbox_comment(), create_if_comment_column(), and process_mbox_data() from Haotian's version of Kaiaulu will not be refactored into Kaiaulu due to ambiguity on the reliance of removing/editing rows depending on the columns reply_id and reply_subject, also purpose deemed unnecessary for Kaiaulu. - Determine what columns in a reply table the soon-to-be refactored python functions into Kaiaulu will apply pre-processing cleaning to. - parse_mbox() currently does two things: parses mail and columns into a reply table. To seperate concerns, parse_mbox() will be modified to just parse, and parse_mbox_replies() will be created to map columns into a reply table (To follow the already established architecture of parse_jira(), parse_jira_replies() and parse_github(), parse_github_replies()) ## Post-meeting issue specification for 11/6/25 - Architecture 3 proposed to address the ping pong concern of Architecture 2.
